title: The best AI investing apps in 2026, compared
summary: Our ranked view of the best AI investing apps in 2026, with prices, who each fits and their limits. We make Astor, one of the apps listed.
body_markdown:
## The best AI investing apps, ranked


### 1. Astor


**What it is.** A[personal investing agent](https://www.astor.app/blog/what-is-a-personal-investing-agent) . It connects to your brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts at most major US institutions, follows every position and the earnings dates, filings and headlines that touch them, and[texts you](https://www.astor.app/blog/talk-to-astor-in-imessage) what happened and why it matters to you. With[Text to Trade](https://www.astor.app/blog/introducing-text-to-trade) , available on Max plans, you approve each trade and orders execute in your own Robinhood agentic account.


**Price.** Free to start with no card. Pro is $19 a month or $10 a month billed yearly, and Max is $29 a month or $19 a month billed yearly.


**Best for.** People who already invest, often across a few accounts, and want something watching what they own while they make the calls. Gaus, Inc. DBA Astor is an SEC-registered investment adviser, so its recommendations are personalized advice.


**Limits.** iPhone and iMessage only, US only. No budgeting, tax filing or estate planning, and it doesn’t run a managed portfolio. The AI can be wrong, which is why it shows its sources.


### 2. Origin


**What it is.** An all-in-one money app with budgeting, spending, net worth, forecasting and investing, plus an AI Advisor that runs proactive checks across your finances and surfaces prioritized Actions. Advisory services come from Origin Investment Advisory LLC, an SEC-registered adviser, and Origin says its AI advice is non-discretionary.


**Price.** $99 a year. As of October 2026, new users can get the first year for $1 as a limited-time offer.


**Best for.** People who want their whole financial life in one app, including those on Android, the web or a Mac.


**Limits.** It’s built for your whole financial picture, so if you only want help with investments, much of the app won’t apply to you. See[Astor vs. Origin](https://www.astor.app/blog/astor-vs-origin) .


### 3. Public


**What it is.** A brokerage that calls itself agentic. It has Alpha, a free AI research tool; Agents, which monitor markets and can trade stocks, options and crypto once you sign off on them; and Generated Assets, which turns a prompt into an index you can invest in.


**Price.** The core account is free, with $0 commissions on stocks and ETFs in regular hours (other fees can apply). Reserve is $20 a month. Generated Assets accounts cost 0.49% a year with a $1,000 minimum.


**Best for.** Investors who want to hold, trade and automate in one app, and who are comfortable with agents acting on rules without approving each trade.


**Limits.** The AI is built around your Public account, and Public says its agentic outputs are informational and illustrative.


### 4. Robinhood (Cortex Assistant and Agents)


**What it is.** Cortex Assistant is a conversational AI in the Robinhood iOS app for Gold members. It can analyze your portfolio, create watchlists and alerts, and pre-fill orders that you confirm. Robinhood Agents, announced in September 2026 for eligible US customers, lets you build an agent that researches and trades in a dedicated agentic account, with trade approvals on by default.


**Price.** Cortex Assistant comes with Robinhood Gold, at $5 a month after a 30-day free trial. Agents run on prepaid tokens, starting with a free balance.


**Best for.** People who keep most of their investing at Robinhood.


**Limits.** It works with your Robinhood accounts, Robinhood says Cortex Assistant isn’t an investment adviser, and Agents’ approvals can be switched off. More in[AI trading on Robinhood](https://www.astor.app/blog/ai-trading-strategy-robinhood) .


### 5. Range


**What it is.** Full-service wealth management. You work with a team of advisers, including CFPs and CFA charterholders, supported by an AI called Rai, and Range manages your investments through a discretionary agreement. Range Advisory, LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser.


**Price.** Flat annual fees of $3,950 (Premium), $5,950 (Platinum) or $12,500 (Titanium), with no asset-based advisory fee. Third-party fees can apply.


**Best for.** Households who want people, tax planning and estate work in one relationship, and want someone else to run the portfolio.


**Limits.** It costs thousands of dollars a year, and you hand off the investment decisions.


### 6. Perplexity Finance


**What it is.** Perplexity’s finance research features. Since early 2026 you can link brokerage accounts read-only through Plaid and ask about your holdings, with basic portfolio features free. As of Perplexity’s April 2026 update, it was on desktop in the US and Canada.


**Price.** Free. Pro is $20 a month and Max is $200 a month, and the more advanced agent features are limited to those plans.


**Best for.** Fast, sourced research on companies and markets.


**Limits.** Perplexity’s terms say not to rely on its output for investment or financial advice. See[Astor vs. Perplexity Finance](https://www.astor.app/blog/astor-vs-perplexity-finance) .


### 7. ChatGPT


**What it is.** ChatGPT’s Finances feature lets US users connect accounts through Plaid and ask about spending, net worth and investments, with a dashboard that includes portfolio allocation and daily changes in your stock and ETF holdings.


**Price.** Finances is available on every US plan. ChatGPT is free, Go is $8 a month, Plus is $20 a month and Pro starts at $100 a month.


**Best for.** General money questions in a tool you may already use, on the web, iPhone or Android.


**Limits.** OpenAI says ChatGPT isn’t a fiduciary, registered investment adviser or broker-dealer, and it can’t make trades. More in[Astor vs. ChatGPT](https://www.astor.app/blog/astor-vs-chatgpt) .


### 8. Betterment and Wealthfront


**What they are.** Robo-advisors. You pick a goal and risk level, and they invest and rebalance a portfolio for you. Betterment’s custom portfolios include AI insights on diversification and sector exposure, which Betterment says don’t include recommendations or factor in your outside accounts.


**Price.** Wealthfront charges 0.25% a year with a $500 minimum. Betterment charges $5 a month on balances under $24,000 (unless you deposit at least $200 a month) and 0.25% a year from $24,000, with lower rates above $1 million.


**Best for.** Hands-off investors who want a diversified portfolio managed for them.


**Limits.** You move money into their accounts to have it managed, so the help centers on what you invest with them. See[Astor vs. Wealthfront](https://www.astor.app/blog/astor-vs-wealthfront) and[Astor vs. Betterment](https://www.astor.app/blog/astor-vs-betterment) .
